facts: On the south bank of the Brisbane River just south of South Bank, near Goodwill Bridge
Collection includes WW2 frigate HMAS Diamantina, Carpentaria Light Ship, small boats, a dry dock, lighthouses and marine engines
brisbane-11.notes: Adult $18 from the museum's Visit page (child $8, family $42-50, concession $15). Page title names the museum.

facts: Heritage-listed storehouse at 115 William Street, built 1828-29 by convict labour for the Moreton Bay penal settlement
One of only two buildings surviving from the penal colony; run as a museum by the Royal Historical Society of Queensland
Closed Saturday to Monday
brisbane-12.notes: Adult $12 (concession $9, child $5, family $24) from the museum's own homepage. Older third-party pages show $7-$10; ignored.

facts: Museum of Brisbane's wartime heritage, 1942-45, in MacArthur Chambers (former AMP building) on Queen and Edward Streets; entrance via Edward Street
On level 8, where General MacArthur's HQ was set up in 1942; opened 5 October 2004
brisbane-13.notes: Adult $10 (senior $5, child $5, family $20) from mmb.org.au, whose title names the museum. Site says open Tue, Thu, Sun only: put in bio/tip if needed, not as hours. Wikipedia has no article (wiki null is right).
unverified: Entry level 8 detail and address from a search summary only (anzacsquare.qld.gov.au / placesofpride.awm.gov.au); both fetched OK for AWM page

facts: In Brisbane Botanic Gardens Mt Coot-tha; centrepiece is the Cosmic Skydome with fulldome shows of the night sky and universe
Display Zone, Sundial Courtyard and gift shop are free to visit; shows are ticketed
brisbane-14.notes: Council page: 'You can visit the Planetarium for free, but charges apply for shows'. Adult Cosmic Skydome general show $17.50 (concession $13.50). Council page is the operator's page.
unverified: Council page notes closures 9-11 and 23-27 Nov 2026 (not recorded as hours)

facts: Heritage-listed cliffs at Kangaroo Point across the river from the CBD, popular for rock climbing and running
Reached on foot from South Bank, Kangaroo Point Green Bridge or Story Bridge, or by ferry to Holman Street or Maritime Museum terminals
Council lists Kangaroo Point Cliffs Park (River Terrace Park) with Cliffs Boardwalk, kayak hire and climbing; open 24 hours at River Terrace entrance
brisbane-16.notes: Open public park; no entry fee. Metered street parking not a cost. Council page is a parks-by-suburb list, not a single steward page, so no ticketUrl.

facts: Heritage-listed riverfront park, designed by Albert Herbert Foster, built 1914-1950, on the Queensland Heritage Register since 7 Feb 2005
Council page lists picnic shelters, electric barbecues, playgrounds, library, tennis courts and a coffee kiosk; free parking on the internal ring road
brisbane-17.notes: Brisbane City Council public park, no entry fee. Council page exists (https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/parks-and-recreation/parks-and-greenspaces/find-park-facilities-and-locations/new-farm-park) but it is a park-booking page; left out of ticketUrl as an open park.
unverified: Category 'entertainment' on input looks wrong for a park; orchestrator may recategorise

facts: Jetty at 139 Redcliffe Parade, Redcliffe, on Moreton Bay; popular fishing spot
Dates to 1885; current (third) jetty began construction in 1995, jutting from the site of a 1930s bathing pavilion (from search summary of local history article)
brisbane-19.notes: Open public jetty. Listing on visit.brisbane.qld.au (ATDW) fetched OK, address confirmed; no single operator site. Wikipedia has no article. Category 'beach' on input is a poor fit.
unverified: 1885/1995 history from search summary only (moretondaily.com.au); not fetched

facts: Queensland's first historic national park (created 1990 per Wikipedia), main attraction Fort Lytton Historic Military Precinct with guided tours, museum and re-enactments
Pentagonal 19th-century fort with guns behind grassy ramparts; park extended in 1999
Search summary of QPWS visitor guide: open Sundays and most public holidays, ~90-minute tours; weekday visits booked, adult $7.60
brisbane-22.notes: Cost low confidence: Visit Brisbane (ATDW) listing says 'Experience is free'; search summary of the QPWS visitor guide says Sunday entry free but weekday guided visits adult $7.60. QPWS pages 403 to scripts; browser check needed to confirm price/free and the park-pass question (Queensland has no day-use national park entry pass). If weekday tour is the standard price, costMin/Max 7.60 'tour'.
unverified: Entry fee/Sunday-free vs weekday $7.60 (QPWS page BLOCKED)
Whether any Queensland pass applies (none expected)

facts: Run by Queensland Parks and Wildlife Service at Daisy Hill Conservation Park; wild koalas seen up close
Free admission, free ranger talks (about 11am and 2pm per search summary); surrounding walking tracks
brisbane-24.notes: QPWS about page states 'Free admission' (fetched OK). Page title names the centre. No pass applies. Category 'viewpoint' on input is wrong (wildlife centre).
unverified: Talk times from search summary only

facts: Heritage-listed zoological garden at 28 Tomewin Street, Currumbin, built from 1947 (Queensland Heritage Register 2009)
Known for feeding flocks of free-flying wild rainbow lorikeets; feeding at 8am and 4pm is free to watch with no ticket
gold-coast-2.notes: Adult general admission $70 from the sanctuary's Visit page (first price column; concession $55, youth $50). Home page title names the sanctuary. A BOGO promo runs 6 Nov-5 Dec 2026, ignored.
unverified: Second price column ($125) not identified (likely a pass/combo); $70 taken as general entry
